beats.headline: White instead of red
beats.text: Sifting through his rewards, Carl finds more goblin dynamite and smoke bombs, and, in the bronze boss box from his fight with Heather, a whole box of hobgoblin dynamite along with three globs of Hobgoblin Pus, the remote-controlled explosive detonators. He has never seen hobgoblin dynamite before. The sticks are white instead of red, with a larger yield, and they are much more stable.

beats.headline: Highway robbery
beats.text: Pustule's tables at the Silk Road hold boxes of goblin and hobgoblin dynamite, smoke bombs, detonators and pancake-like claymores at 5,000 gold each. A case of goblin dynamite is twenty-five sticks for 500 gold. The hobgoblin sticks are twenty for 2,000, which Carl calls highway robbery. Her fused hob-lobbers, she says, work like hobgoblin dynamite: impact resistant, extra stable, light the fuse and toss.

beats.headline: Practically mini nukes
beats.text: From a rooftop near the saferoom, Carl does not want to waste his hob-lobbers on a handful of shambling berserkers, so he tries a stick of hobgoblin dynamite, which he has never used. He hurls it with his upgraded strength at a shambler half a block away. The explosion knocks him off his feet, the front of a distant building caves in and fills the street with debris, and the shambler and the one behind it are obliterated. The power is great, he decides, but the sticks are utterly impractical in regular fights.

beats.headline: Two robots, three sticks
beats.text: For the two robots, Carl uses three sticks of hobgoblin dynamite and a detonator. He sets the charges without incident, moves all the way back to the platform and sets them off. The automatons never turned on or fought back, and they come back as scrap, their bottom halves mostly intact and hunks of metal everywhere: the hobgoblin dynamite is especially good at tearing stuff up. Once the metal cools he collects all he can, cogs, wheels and two damaged dwarven batteries.

beats.headline: A stick in every mine
beats.text: Carl's new mines look like tire-shaped cross sections of the spiked naval contact mines of the early twentieth century, the plunger lifted from the cookbook and changed just enough. Each is an oblong metal tube stuffed with hob-lobbers, with a single, hopefully stable stick of hobgoblin dynamite added for extra measure. When a train depresses a spike, an impact-detonated hob-lobber shatters and the whole mine shreds. The system calls it a Jelly Bomb, and gives him no credit for inventing it.

beats.headline: A train full of explosives
beats.text: Elle tells Carl by chat that some crazy asshole is throwing a train full of explosives their way. He laughs and ties the last piece of hobgoblin dynamite onto the pile. It is much more stable than the goblin stuff and should, in theory, survive multiple impacts, and the bundle rides up high so it won't go off until triggered: a long pole with an impact-detonated hob-lobber at the end, too high for the ordinary blister ghouls, low enough for a giant stage-three monster, or the back of the other train.

beats.headline: A block per barrel
beats.text: They jump into burning, smoky chaos. The whole block is on fire and blown apart, a thick fog fills the air and bodies are everywhere. Carl's barrel explosives were crammed with gunpowder, hobgoblin dynamite and delay-detonated smoke curtains, packed for the most destruction: unstable as anything, but a single one can take out an entire block. They lived only because they hid inside a real saferoom.

beats.headline: Over the trench
beats.text: Cries for shields run up and down the trench as giant, exploding monsters close in, and arrows, bolts and spears do nothing to them. Heads up, Carl calls, pulls a stick of full-strength hobgoblin dynamite and tosses it over the edge like a grenade. Everyone ducks and covers their ears. The blast rocks the ground, experience notifications fly by with a new achievement, and through the periscope the ones immediately in front are gone, though more keep coming. He prepares a second stick.
